data.content_ref: inline:The mechanism is internally self-defeating. It elaborates an elaborate Popperian apparatus — the corroboration/probability distinction, the asymmetry of falsification, the methodological rule to maximize verisimilitude — and then concludes with a flat non sequitur: 'It follows that the underlying structure was never relevant to the outcome at all.' But the entire preceding mechanism IS the underlying structure that produces the outcome (the preference for better-corroborated theories). The asymmetry of falsification, the logical report of test severity, and the conjectural status of verisimilitude are precisely the structural features the mechanism invokes to justify the preference. If those structures are 'never relevant,' then the mechanism has no basis for its own conclusion, and the claim's defense of Popper collapses into arbitrariness even on its own terms — not because of an external objection about induction or the Tichý/Miller proof (already raised), but because the argument's internal reasoning contradicts its own conclusion.
